claims.text: Before starting, set the seat to a comfortable height, adjust the machine to line up with your torso, and choose the weight.

quotes.text: Adjust the seat to a comfortable height and the weight to the appropriate level before beginning.
Adjust machine for proper alignment with torso.

claims.text: Sit with the hips pressed against the back of the seat and the shins pushed against the padded roller, abs tight.

quotes.text: Sitting with the hips pressed against the back of the seat, push the shins against the padded roller and tighten the abs.

claims.text: Hold the handles in both hands (elbows bent about 90 degrees on some machines; on others the handles are overhead and keep the pads on the shoulders).

quotes.text: Grasp the handles in both hands, and pull down on them to lean forward.
grasp the handles with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
grabbing ahold of the handles overhead to place a pad on your shoulders.

claims.text: Crunch forward by flexing (curling) the spine until the ribs come toward the pelvis, breathing out; then return slowly.

quotes.text: Brace core and exhale as you crunch forward by flexing spine.
Flex spine until ribs approach pelvis, then return until arms are extended but without full relaxation.
Flex the bottom of your ribcage into your belly button

claims.text: Return slowly and keep tension: don't let the weight stack come to rest between reps.

quotes.text: Return slowly to the starting position.
Maintain tension without letting weight stack rest.

claims.text: Avoid excessive weight to prevent back strain; people with spinal conditions should get professional advice.

quotes.text: Avoid excessive weight to prevent back strain
Consult professional for spinal conditions

claims.text: Breathe out on the crunch and in on the return.

quotes.text: Exhale during the crunch and inhale on the return.

claims.text: The abdominal muscles do the bending; the machine crunch targets the rectus abdominis.

quotes.text: Bend forward by contracting your abs.
Seated machine isolation exercise that targets the rectus abdominis

claims.text: Measured on a seated crunch machine (Technogym, 10 RM): rectus abdominis 84% of max and rectus femoris (a hip flexor) 65%, versus 104% and 27% for an elastic-band Swiss-ball crunch; across both, the rectus abdominis and external obliques were the most active muscles.

quotes.text: crunches on Swiss ball with elastic resistance showed higher activity of the rectus abdominis than crunches performed on the machine (104±3.8 vs 84±3.8% nEMG respectively, P<0.0001).
crunches performed on Swiss ball induced lower activity of the rectus femoris than crunches in training machine (27±3.7 vs 65±3.8% nEMG respectively, P<0.0001)
normalized EMG was highest in the rectus abdominis (P<0.01) and the external obliques (P<0.01).

claims.text: The study authors say the machine's lower abdominal and higher hip-flexor activity warrants caution for people with lower back pain.

quotes.text: the lower rectus abdominis activity and higher rectus femoris activity observed in machine warrant caution for individuals with lumbar pain.

claims.text: By reasoning from c4 and c9, not a measured fault rate: folding forward at the hips with a flat back, instead of curling the ribs toward the pelvis, shifts work to the hip flexors, which were already highly active on the machine.

quotes.text: Flex spine until ribs approach pelvis
higher rectus femoris activity observed in machine

claims.text: Tempo: moderate speed, about 1-2 s each way, with a slow return.

quotes.text: at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC)
Return slowly to the starting position.

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

plate.viewWhy: Spinal flexion is a sagittal-plane movement and reads only from the side (census: side). The drawn fault, hinging at the hips with a flat back (c11), also needs the side view.
plate.equipment: Seated crunch machine (composed, census R3): seat with back pad, padded shin roller, handles on a pivoting arm by the shoulders (c2, c3). Floor line.
plate.start: Seated upright, hips pressed against the back of the seat, shins against the roller (c2), hands on the handles (c3), abs tight (c2).
plate.end: Spine curled forward so the ribs come toward the pelvis (c4); hips still back in the seat (c2).

checkpoints.label: Hips back
checkpoints.what: Hips stay pressed against the back of the seat.

checkpoints.label: Curl the spine
checkpoints.what: Bend by curling the ribs toward the pelvis.

checkpoints.label: Shins on roller
checkpoints.what: Shins pushed against the padded roller.

mistake.what: Hinging at the hips: the torso tips forward with a flat back instead of curling.
mistake.why: The sources cue curling the spine; the machine already showed high hip-flexor activity (c9), and a flat-back hinge shifts more work to the hip flexors. No source ranks how common it is; this is reasoning (MECH/WEAK).

tells.text: Hips stay back in the seat

plate.variantLine: Crunch machines differ: ACE's has a shin roller and handles you pull down (c2, c3); Fitbod's has overhead handles with pads on the shoulders (c3). Drawn: shin roller and handles by the shoulders. Claims c1, c4-c13 hold for both.

handlingMistakes.fix: Lower the weight to protect your back.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Tipping forward from the hips with a flat back.
handlingMistakes.fix: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Letting the weight stack rest between reps.
handlingMistakes.fix: Keep tension; return without letting the stack rest.

rows.means: The abs are doing the work.
Usually means the hip flexors are taking over.
rows.fix: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis.

rows.means: Usually means the weight is too heavy.
rows.fix: Stop the set; lower the weight next time.

risks.risk: Too much weight can strain the back.
High hip-flexor work on the machine calls for caution with lower back pain.

zooms.right: Spine curled, ribs coming toward the pelvis.
zooms.wrong: Back flat, torso tipping forward from the hips.

zooms.wrong: Hips sliding forward off the seat back.

libraryDiff.why: abs primary is sourced (c8, c9). obliques added as secondary: external obliques were among the most active muscles (c9, measured across both crunch types). hip_flexors added as secondary: rectus femoris reached 65% of max on the machine (c9, DATA).
